catalog_quote: In this chapter we discuss the position and internal subgrouping of the Aru languages. For this, we rely almost entirely on Nivens (2017), a database of over 900 Proto-Aru reconstructions with supporting reflexes. All data and Proto-Aru reconstructions in this chapter are from this database with some differences in the analysis of the Proto-Aru phoneme inventory. ... Karey, Lorang, Mariri, and Kompane are only spoken in one village each. Transcriptions of data are adapted to IPA standards, with the following exceptions. The letter ‹y› is used for the palatal glide [j], Tarangan mid-close [e] and [o] are transcribed ‹ê› and ‹ô› (mid-open [ɛ] and [ɔ] are transcribed ‹ɛ› and ‹ɔ›), and unexpected stress is marked by an acute accent. (The normal pattern is penultimate stress, or final stress if the final syllable contains a mid-vowel.) ... [p. 88:] Informed clarifications are extremely helpf…

new_statements.rule_in_words: For the Aru data set as a whole (Karey included), the default is stress on the penultimate syllable, shifting to the final syllable when that syllable contains a mid vowel; words that deviate are individually marked with an acute in Nivens's database, and about ten cited Karey forms carry such marks (several with final stress on a non-mid vowel, e.g. ŋamár, kanáβir, etú, or antepenultimate, e.g. gíbado, góliŋ), so stress in Karey is largely but not fully predictable.
new_statements.exceptions: Lexically marked exceptions in the Karey data: ŋamár 'sky', gíbado, ʤáŋel, ʤúor, kanáβir, orwéw, etú, -wólar, gáger, góliŋ, kartáo 'mouse/rat?' (acute = stress not predicted by the penult/final-mid-vowel default).
new_statements.domain_note: Citation forms in a comparative wordlist database; a transcription convention covering all 14 Aru lects, not a phonological analysis of Karey; no discussion of phrase vs word level.
new_statements.identity_note: The Grimes & Edwards / Nivens data are labelled 'Karey [kyd] kare1339' (Karey village, east coast of Trangan) and match the target exactly; but the stress rule quoted is a convention stated for all 14 Aru lects in Nivens's database, not for Karey specifically. Note Wattimury et al. 1995 use 'bahasa Tarangan Timur' for Karey, whereas Hughes 1987 and Glottolog treat East Tarangan (east2465, [tre]) as a separate language surrounding the Karey enclave.

sources.note: p. 273: transcription convention for all Aru data incl. Karey: unexpected stress marked with an acute; 'The normal pattern is penultimate stress, or final stress if the final syllable contains a mid-vowel.' Karey forms flagged as deviating: ŋamár 'sky' (p.275), gíbado, ʤáŋel (p.278), ʤúor (p.282), kanáβir, orwéw (p.284), etú (p.286), -wólar (p.287), gáger, góliŋ (p.288), kartáo (appendix); unmarked Karey forms (lado, anido, manua, negen, gwaŋur..) are penultimate by the convention. Second-hand, database-wide, not a Karey-specific description.
